rita: Quick sync — earlier RFCs split handshake vs runtime resolution too much. I'd like to propose a single "session manifest" that is minimal, signed, and negotiable. Key goals: simple routing, explicit capability negotiation, and clear failure classes.

omar: +1 to minimality. Can we define what 'minimal' means? My vote: tenant_hash, affinity_hint, secret_locator (opaque), manifest_version, caps_allowed. Keep TTL low.

kevin: Implementation constraints: hosted cannot receive raw key material. Private/on-prem may allow inline. So secret_locator must be opaque URI (kms://..., local://path, customer-token://). The runtime must only resolve based on capability negotiation.

sec-bot: policy-check: default hosted policy = no_inline_keys, require signed manifest, audit_nonce present. Any manifest that includes inline keys must be allowlisted and security-reviewed.

rita: Draft manifest example (compact):
```json
{"tenant_hash":"th-9f2f","affinity_hint":"zone-2","secret_locator":"kms://r/abcd","ttl":240,"resolve_strategy":"on-demand","caps_allowed":["resolve_kms","cache_creds"],"manifest_v":"2","audit_nonce":"n-73"}
```

omar: We should add capability negotiation step: control plane issues manifest_v + caps_allowed; adapter replies with caps_supported and resolve_intent (eager|lazy|external). If adapter doesn't support manifest_v it must return MANIFEST_UNSUPPORTED immediately.

kevin: Error classes for resolution: RESOLVE_RETRYABLE, RESOLVE_PERMANENT, RESOLVE_POLICY_VIOLATION. Map behaviors: RETRYABLE -> exponential backoff; PERMANENT -> immediate fallback route (if fallback_policy provided) or abort; POLICY_VIOLATION -> abort + audit.

rita: Fallback policies: degrade_to_small_model, route_to_hosted_pool, fail_request. Manifest may include fallback_hint. Also include migration fields: migration_id and grace_seconds for affinity moves so KV caches can be warmed.

omar: Telemetry: include telemetry_tag = HMAC(tenant_id, rotation_key) so adapters can emit traces without exposing tenant. Also manifest should include caps_hash to verify capabilities weren't tampered with.

kevin: Private mode nuance: runtime should never, under any circumstance, attempt to resolve host-managed kms:// URIs. Instead, manifest should carry local:// paths or customer-token:// short-lived tokens. Document this as a hard rule.

sec-bot: checklist: signed_manifest, audit_nonce, ttl <= 600s, caps_allowed explicit, telemetry_tag present. Any violation -> manifest rejected.

rita: Migration sketch: control plane issues new manifest with migration_id + grace_seconds; old adapter continues serving until grace_seconds expire, after which control plane switches routing. During grace window adapters may pre-warm caches.

omar: One more for ops: require a ManifestResolution event in tracing with manifest_id, resolution_result, error_class. That will make debugging much easier.

kevin: Action items: 1) I'll draft the JSON Schema for manifest_v=2 and example adapters, 2) omar write the RBAC/KMS resolution matrix for hosted/dedicated/private, 3) rita will assemble an RFC with error classes and migration flow. I'll also prototype a small harness that simulates RESOLVE_RETRYABLE and RESOLVE_PERMANENT.

deploy-bot: ci: manifest-schema-tests queued, migration-sim started.

rita: Cool — will open RFC draft tomorrow. If anyone has objections, drop here. Otherwise quick :thumbsup:.

omar: :thumbsup:  

kevin: :thumbsup:  

sec-bot: policy-note: secure review required for any manifest containing inline key material.
